name: Chives
imageAlt: Illustration of chives with thin green blades and round purple flowers
description: A tidy perennial with slender, hollow green leaves and a mild onion flavor. In late spring chives produce round purple pom-pom flowers that are edible and attract pollinators.
uses: Snipped over eggs, potatoes and soups
Mixed into cream cheese, sour cream dips and butters
Edible flowers for salads and vinegars
Finishing herb for fish and baked potatoes
Traditionally eaten to stimulate the appetite and help digestion
Used in folk cooking to add flavor while reducing the need for salt
Sulfur compounds in the allium family were used in folk medicine for colds
benefits: Good source of vitamin K, and also provides vitamin C, vitamin A and folate
Contains flavonoid antioxidants and sulfur compounds
Adds flavor with almost no calories
medicinal.caution: Chives are rich in vitamin K, so people on blood thinners such as warfarin should keep their intake steady. Chives and other alliums are toxic to cats and dogs, so keep them out of reach of pets.

video.title: How to Plant and Grow Perennial Chives

taste: Mild, fresh and savory, like a gentle spring onion.
sideEffects: Large amounts can upset the stomach or cause gas
The high vitamin K content can affect blood thinners

safety.allergy: Chives belong to the onion family. People allergic to onions, garlic or leeks may react to chives.
safety.pregnancy: Normal food amounts are considered safe.
safety.pets: Chives, like onions and garlic, are toxic to cats and dogs and can damage their red blood cells. Keep pets away from the plant.
safety.medications: Chives contain vitamin K, so people on warfarin should keep their intake steady and ask their doctor.

temperature: Extremely hardy. Chives survive winter cold of about -30 °C, die back in winter and regrow in spring. They grow best at about 15-25 °C.
harvest: Cut the leaves 2-5 cm above the ground with scissors, starting when they are about 15 cm tall. Harvest the outer leaves first or cut the whole clump back and it will regrow. Pick the flowers just as they open.
storage: Keep fresh chives in a glass of water or in a bag in the fridge for one to two weeks. Chop and freeze them for later. Drying loses most of their flavor.
dailyLife: Snip over scrambled eggs, baked potatoes and soups
Stir into cream cheese, sour cream or yogurt dips
Scatter the purple flowers over salads
Use instead of salt to add flavor
tips: Divide clumps every three or four years to keep them strong
Cut flower stems if you want more leaves
Plant near carrots and tomatoes as a companion

origin.region: Europe, Asia and North America (cool northern regions)
origin.details: Chives grow wild across the cooler parts of Europe, Asia and North America. They are the only onion-family plant found naturally on both sides of the Atlantic.
